h1: UK Passport Photo Requirements — Free Online Checker, Crop & Size Tool
content:
Meet Every British Passport Photo Requirement — Instantly Online

Getting your UK passport photo wrong is one of the most common reasons passport applications are delayed or rejected. Our free tool checks your photo against all official British passport photo specifications — dimensions, background colour, head size, lighting, and expression — and corrects any issues automatically. Upload your existing photo or take a new one, select UK Passport, and download a print-ready or digital file that fully meets passport photo requirements UK authorities enforce. No Photoshop. No photo booth queue. No software to install.

How to Create a Compliant UK Passport Photo — 3 Steps

  1. Upload Your Photo: Drag and drop any photo from your phone or camera. JPEG, PNG, and HEIC files are all accepted — no conversion needed. Maximum file size is 20 MB.
  2. Auto-Check & Fix: Our tool runs 30+ compliance checks against official UK passport photo standard rules — head position, eye line, background colour, lighting, and resolution — and corrects issues automatically.
  3. Download Print or Digital File: Get a print-ready 6×4 inch template with four passport photos, or a single digital file at the correct pixel dimensions for online renewal submissions. Both formats meet UK passport photo size requirements for HMPO and gov.uk applications.

Official UK Passport Photo Size and Specifications

The UK government publishes strict British passport photo guidelines that every application must meet. Below are the current official passport photo specifications UK applicants must follow for both printed and digital submissions.

Specification Printed Photo Digital Photo
Dimensions 35mm × 45mm (passport photo size UK cm: 3.5 × 4.5 cm) 600 × 750 pixels minimum
UK passport photo size in inches 1.37" × 1.77" N/A (pixel-based)
Aspect ratio 7:9 (passport photo ratio UK) 7:9
Resolution 600 DPI minimum UK passport photo size in pixels: min 600 × 750 px
Head height 29–34mm (chin to crown) 70–80% of frame height
Background Plain cream or white — UK passport size photo background colour Plain cream or white
File format (digital) N/A JPEG only, max 10 MB

Full British Passport Photo Checklist

Beyond dimensions, the photo requirements for British passport applications cover expression, clothing, and face visibility. Our tool checks all of the following automatically.

  • Face fully visible: No hair, hats, or scarves over your face. Religious head coverings are accepted but must not cast shadows.
  • Neutral expression: Mouth closed, eyes open, looking directly at the camera. No smiling.
  • No glasses: Passport photos ban all eyewear, including prescription glasses and sunglasses.
  • Plain background: Cream or light grey, with no shadows, patterns, or other people visible.
  • Even lighting: No shadows on the face or background.
  • Recent likeness: Taken within the last month.

UK Driving Licence Photo Requirements

DVLA driving licence photos follow the same 35 × 45mm biometric standard as passports, but two rules work differently — and both trip people up.

Can I wear glasses for my driving licence photo? Yes. Unlike a passport photo, DVLA rules let you keep your glasses on if you normally wear them. The only conditions: your eyes must be clearly visible, the frames must not cover them, and there must be no tint, glare, or reflection on the lenses. Sunglasses are never accepted. If the DVLA's automated scanner flags glare, the safest fix is to remove your glasses and retake the photo.

Driving licence photo size UK: 35mm wide × 45mm tall for a printed photo, or 600 × 750 pixels for a digital upload — identical to the passport spec, with the same 29–34mm head height and plain light-coloured background.

How many photos for a provisional driving licence? It depends on how you apply. Apply online via GOV.UK and you only need a digital photo upload — no printed copy required, and DVLA can often pull one from your passport record automatically. Apply by post using the D1 form and you need exactly one printed passport-style photo, signed on the back by a countersignatory if DVLA cannot verify your identity electronically. First provisional applications follow the same rules as renewals — there is no separate standard for new drivers.

What Are ICAO Biometric Photo Standards?

ICAO Document 9303 is the international standard behind almost every biometric ID photo, including UK passports, visas, and driving licences. It defines the technical rules that let facial recognition software read a photo reliably: head position and size within the frame, eye height, lighting uniformity, and image sharpness.

How to get an ICAO-compliant photo: face the camera directly with a neutral expression, keep both ears and the full face visible, use even lighting with no shadows or red-eye, and shoot against a plain, unpatterned light background. HMPO and UKVI then layer their own UK-specific rules — cream or light grey background, no glasses, and a maximum one-month photo age — on top of the base ICAO framework. Our built-in ICAO photo checker validates both layers in one pass, so a single upload satisfies the international standard and the UK-specific one together.

UK Visa Photo Requirements, Including Tourist Visas

UK tourist visa photo requirements match the standard 35 × 45mm biometric format used for Standard Visitor visas, Skilled Worker visas, Student visas, and family visas alike. For online applications through the UKVI portal or the UK ID Check app, you upload a digital JPEG of at least 600 × 750 pixels, sized between 50KB and 6MB, on a plain light-coloured background. If your visa route requires a biometric appointment or a postal submission, bring printed 35 × 45mm photos instead — check your specific appointment letter, since some visa centres request more than one print.

As with passports, glasses are not permitted in a UK visa photo, and the photo must be a true, unedited likeness with no digital retouching beyond background correction.

Digital vs Printed — UK Passport Photo Size Digital Explained

Since HMPO introduced the digital renewal pathway, many applicants now need a uk passport digital photo rather than a printed one. If you are renewing online via gov.uk, you will be asked to submit a digital photo or use the government's own UK passport online photo checker. Our tool generates both formats from a single upload — a digital JPEG at the correct UK passport photo size digital specification, and a printable 6×4 sheet for post applications or countersignature submissions.

The UK digital passport photo requirements differ slightly from printed ones: the file must be JPEG, at least 600 × 750 pixels, under 10 MB, and submitted through the official gov.uk portal or a recognised digital photo service. Our tool outputs a file that meets all of these criteria directly.

Frequently Asked Questions — UK Passport Photo Requirements

Do I need to wear glasses for a driver's licence photo?

No, wearing glasses is optional for a DVLA driving licence photo — it is your choice, not a requirement. If you do wear them, make sure your eyes are fully visible with no glare, shadow, or tint on the lenses. This is one of the few UK ID photos where glasses are allowed at all.

What is the standard UK passport photo size?

35mm wide × 45mm tall (3.5 × 4.5cm) for printed photos, or a minimum of 600 × 750 pixels for digital submissions, both at a 7:9 aspect ratio.

What is the driving licence photo size in the UK?

The same as a passport photo: 35 × 45mm printed, or 600 × 750 pixels digital, with a 29–34mm head height and a plain, light-coloured background.

How many photos do I need for a provisional driving licence?

None if you apply online — it's a digital upload only. By post with the D1 form, you need one printed photo, countersigned if DVLA cannot verify your identity another way.

How do I get an ICAO-compliant photo?

Use a plain light background, face forward with a neutral expression, keep your full face and both ears visible, and avoid shadows or glare. Our checker verifies your photo against ICAO Doc 9303 automatically before you download it.

What are the UK tourist visa photo requirements?

A 35 × 45mm biometric photo (or 600 × 750px digital upload), plain light background, neutral expression, and no glasses — the same standard used across most UK visa categories, including Standard Visitor visas.

What background colour does a UK passport photo need?

Plain cream or light grey, with no patterns, shadows, or objects behind you. Our tool replaces your background automatically to meet this rule.

Can I use this tool as an ICAO photo checker for other documents?

Yes. Beyond UK passports, visas, and driving licences, the same ICAO-based checks apply to most biometric ID photos worldwide — select your document type after upload for the matching size profile.

Can I use an online tool as a UK passport photo checker?

Yes. Our free UK passport photo checker online free tool validates your photo against all official HMPO biometric criteria before you submit. It checks dimensions, head position, background colour, lighting, and expression — and shows exactly which criteria pass or fail.

What are the UK passport renewal photo requirements?

The uk passport renewal photo requirements are identical to those for a new passport application — 35×45mm printed or 600×750px digital, plain white/cream background, neutral expression, no glasses, and taken within the last month. Our tool also supports passport photo renewal uk digital submissions via the gov.uk online system.

Does this tool work for UK visa photos too?

Yes — while this page focuses on passport photo requirements UK documents, the same tool also generates compliant photos for UK visa applications. Select your visa type after upload for the correct uk visa photo size and specification profile.

Is a UK passport photo template available to download?

Yes. After checking and correcting your image, you can download a ready-to-print UK passport photo template — a standard 6×4 inch sheet with four correctly sized and spaced photos, formatted for home printing or professional photo labs.

content:
What Is an ICAO Standard Photograph?

The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) sets the global biometric photo standard used by passport authorities, visa offices, and airport identity systems around the world. An ICAO standard photograph follows strict rules for head size, eye position, background color, lighting, and image sharpness so that facial recognition software can read it accurately at border control. Most countries base their national passport photo rules directly on ICAO standards, which is why a photo that meets ICAO specifications is accepted almost everywhere. Our tool builds a fully compliant ICAO standard photograph from any photo you upload, in under a minute, with no design software required.

How to Create an ICAO Compliant Photograph — 3 Steps

You do not need to understand the technical specifications yourself. The tool applies them for you.

  1. Choose Your Document: Select the passport, visa, or ID type you need. The tool loads the exact ICAO-based profile for that document, including biometric ratios, background color, and resolution.
  2. Upload a Photo: Upload an existing photo or take a new one with your phone. JPEG, PNG, and HEIC files all work, from a camera roll, scanner, or gallery.
  3. Auto-Correct and Download: The tool removes the background, replaces it with the required color, aligns your face to the ICAO grid, and checks lighting and sharpness before you download the finished photo.

Core Requirements of an ICAO Standard Photograph

ICAO photo standards exist to make sure a photo works both for a human officer at a counter and for automated facial recognition at an e-gate. The tool checks every one of these points automatically.

  • Head Position and Size: ICAO defines the exact proportion of the frame your head should occupy, measured from chin to crown. The tool uses facial landmark detection to align and crop your photo to this ratio precisely.
  • Neutral Background: A plain, evenly lit background — usually white or light grey — is a core ICAO requirement, since shadows or texture can confuse recognition software. The tool removes your original background and replaces it automatically.
  • Even, Shadow-Free Lighting: ICAO standards reject photos with shadows on the face or background. The tool detects lighting imbalance and corrects it so the final image is uniformly lit.
  • Neutral Expression, Open Eyes: A neutral expression with both eyes open and visible is required under ICAO guidelines. The tool flags photos with closed eyes, tilted heads, or exaggerated expressions so you can retake them if needed.
  • Resolution and Sharpness: ICAO sets a minimum resolution and sharpness threshold to keep facial features clearly readable. The tool outputs at the correct pixel dimensions and DPI for print or digital submission.

ICAO Standard Photograph vs Country-Specific Rules

Every member country of the International Civil Aviation Organization builds its national passport and visa photo rules on the same ICAO foundation, then adds small local variations. The United States, the United Kingdom, Schengen countries, India, and most others follow ICAO proportions for head size and expression, but differ slightly on background shade or final print size.

Selecting your destination country in the tool applies the correct local variation on top of the ICAO base standard, so you get a photo that satisfies both the international standard and the specific authority reviewing your application.

Tips for a Photo That Meets ICAO Standards on the First Try

  • Face a window for soft, natural light and avoid direct sun, which creates hard shadows.
  • Position the camera at eye level, about 1.5 metres away, to keep facial proportions accurate.
  • Keep a neutral expression with your mouth closed and both eyes fully open.
  • Remove glasses, hats, and headphones — ICAO standards restrict most items that cover the face.
  • Pull hair away from your eyes and the outline of your face.
  • Use a plain wall or sheet behind you if possible, so the background removal step has a clean edge to work with.

Official Government References

Verify current photo specifications directly with official international and national government portals:

  • ICAO – International Civil Aviation Organization (Official Site)
  • GOV.UK – Official UK Passport Photo Guidelines
  • Consulate General of India – Passport & Visa Photo Specifications
  • France-Visas – Official Visa Photo Guidelines & FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions About the ICAO Standard Photograph

What does ICAO mean?

ICAO stands for the International Civil Aviation Organization, a United Nations agency that sets global standards for air travel, including the biometric photo specifications used in passports and travel documents. These standards keep facial recognition systems consistent across airports and border checkpoints worldwide.

Is an ICAO standard photograph the same as a passport photo?

Not exactly, though the two overlap heavily. ICAO sets the international baseline for head position, background, lighting, and expression. Individual countries then add their own passport photo rules on top of that baseline, such as a specific print size or background shade.

Which documents require an ICAO standard photograph?

Passports, most visa applications, national ID cards, and airport biometric enrolment programs all rely on ICAO photo standards. The tool covers all of these document types by loading the correct profile once you select your destination.

Can I use an existing photo, or do I need a new one?

An existing photo often works well if your face is clear, well-lit, and facing forward. The tool corrects background, crop, and lighting automatically. If the original has closed eyes, heavy shadow, or extreme head tilt, a fresh photo will produce a more reliable result.

Will an ICAO standard photograph be accepted at every airport and embassy?

A photo built to ICAO standards is accepted by every country that bases its rules on the ICAO framework, which includes nearly all ICAO member states. Selecting your specific country in the tool applies any additional local rule on top of the ICAO baseline for full compliance.

Is it free to create an ICAO standard photograph with this tool?

Yes. Uploading your photo and running the full ICAO compliance check, including background replacement and biometric alignment, is free. A small fee applies only when you download the final high-resolution, watermark-free file.

Core ICAO Photo Standards You Need to Meet

  • Head Coverage: Your face should measure 32mm to 36mm from chin to the top of your hair, centered in the frame.

Common Mistakes That Get an ICAO Photo Rejected

Most rejections come down to a handful of avoidable errors. Watch out for these before you submit your photo:

  • Taking the photo indoors under yellow or dim lighting, which throws off the color balance.
  • Cropping too tight or too loose, so the head-height ratio falls outside the allowed range.

  • Wearing a big smile or tilting the head, both of which count as a non-neutral expression.

Our tool catches each of these automatically, so you fix the issue before you print or submit anything.

What Is a Dubai Visa Photo?

A Dubai visa photo is a biometric-style picture that meets the size, background, and quality rules set by the UAE's Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP) and the General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs, Dubai (GDRFA Dubai). Whether you're applying for a tourist visa, employment visa, residence visa, or an Emirates ID, your dubai visa picture is checked against these official specifications before your application is accepted. Getting the dubai visa photo size or background wrong is one of the most common reasons applications get sent back for resubmission. Our free tool builds a compliant dubai visa pic from any photo you already have, checked against the same rules used by ICP Smart Services and the GDRFA Dubai portal.

How to Create a Dubai Visa Photo in Minutes

  1. Upload a Photo: Stand facing a window or soft natural light, look straight ahead with a neutral expression, and take a photo on your phone.
  2. Run the AI Check: The tool scans head size, eye position, background purity, and lighting, then flags anything that doesn't match the official dubai visa photo specification.
  3. Download Your File: Get a high-resolution, watermark-free dubai visa image sized correctly for online upload or print, ready for VFS, ICP Smart Services, or GDRFA Dubai submission.

Official Dubai Visa Photo Requirements

These specifications apply to tourist, visit, employment, and residence visas processed through GDRFA Dubai and ICP, and they form the baseline for the dubai passport photo requirements most applicants search for.

  • Photo Size: The most commonly cited dubai visa photo dimensions for print submissions are 4.3cm x 5.5cm (43mm x 55mm). Some ICP-linked services instead use the ICAO biometric standard of 3.5cm x 4.5cm (35mm x 45mm) — the same dubai passport size photo dimensions used for the Emirates ID. Because the figure differs by portal, always confirm the exact dubai photo size for visa on the platform you're submitting to before printing.
  • Head Coverage: Your face should fill roughly 70–80% of the frame, measured from the base of the chin to the top of the head.
  • Background: Plain white background with no shadows, patterns, or tint.
  • Expression: Neutral expression, mouth closed, eyes open, looking directly at the camera.
  • Recency: Taken within the last 6 months and reflecting your current appearance.
  • Resolution: Minimum 600 DPI for print; digital uploads typically require around 300 x 369px (GDRFA Dubai) or higher-resolution equivalents for ICP Smart Services.
  • No Accessories: No glasses, hats, or headphones, unless worn daily for religious or medical reasons — even then, eyes must remain fully visible.

Dubai Tourist Visa Photo Requirements vs Other Visa Types

The dubai tourist visa photo requirements are identical to those for employment, residence, and transit visas — there's no separate size or background rule for tourists. The same applies to a dubai visa passport photo size submitted for a dependent or family visa: one clear, forward-facing photo per applicant, with children photographed alone and without toys or other people in frame.

Common Mistakes That Get a Dubai Visa Photo Rejected

  • Submitting the wrong size — mixing up the 43x55mm print format with the 35x45mm ICAO/Emirates ID format.

This is different from the 35mm x 45mm format used for many other countries' visas and from a standard china passport size photo requested for domestic Chinese documents, so don't reuse a leftover photo from another application.
  • Head Width: 15mm to 22mm.
  • Head Height: 28mm to 33mm, measured chin to crown — roughly 70–80% of the photo's height.
  • Head Position: Centered in the frame, tilted no more than about 20° left or right and no more than about 25° up or down.
  • Background: Plain white, with no shadows, patterns, or texture.
  • Clothing: Wear a coloured or dark top — a white top can blend into the background and cause rejection.
  • Expression: Neutral, eyes open, mouth closed, ears visible where possible, no head covering unless worn daily for religious reasons.
